analyst_view.overall: In-form Bologna (8th, four straight wins under Palladino) host bottom side Udinese, who sacked Runjaic on 2 November after eight games without a win and are now coached by Paolo Zanetti, who has had the international break to work with the squad. Bologna miss Holm and Enem and also left-back Juan Miranda (hamstring, back around end of November), their main assist provider, who is not on the numbers' list; Cambiaghi, counted as out, is in a race to be fit after an ankle knock with Italy (reports split). Udinese miss Gueye and Bertola (both counted), while Alaba and Zanoli are close to returning. Referee Livio Marinelli's average card record is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals, already lifted by Bologna's 13 goals in their last 6 and Udinese's leaky defence, and already cut for Cambiaghi and Gueye. Miranda's absence takes away much of Bologna's creativity down the left, and Zanetti is expected to keep a back three that drops into a five, with two weeks to organise it, so a mild lean lower to about 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners. Bologna should have most of the ball against a deep Udinese, which can bring corners, but losing Miranda's crossing works the other way, so nothing points clearly either way and I stay at 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards and already count Marinelli's average record (3.6 per game in 27 games) and Udinese's quiet recent card count. A bottom side under a new coach may defend more aggressively, but Bologna are a calm, possession side, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots, already lifted by both teams' recent shooting. Without Miranda's deliveries and against a Udinese side likely set up to defend in numbers under Zanetti, Bologna may find fewer clean chances, so a small cut to about 25.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target, already lifted 16% by Bologna's sharp recent finishing. Orsolini and Bernardeschi are expected to start and Udinese have conceded plenty on target lately, so I see no reason to move from 8.8.
